# LegatorOCR v0.2.0-pre.13 (pre-release)

Changes since pre.12. Command-line; the window is unchanged.

**Native OCR**
- Curved and tilted text blocks are now traced letter by letter (a parabola fitted per line), so lines of a bent page are read along their real course instead of being cut as flat strips. A fit bug that rejected most curved lines is fixed.
- New model, fine-tuned on 5956 real lines: 2445 of one magazine (ABBYY text layer) plus about 3350 lines of a 1960 textbook and three more magazine issues, labelled where the native engine and Tesseract agree (so they adapt the model to typeface and scanner; they add no new ground truth).
- Measured on pages **not** used for training:
  - 1960 textbook, 5 pages transcribed by hand by the assistant (one reader, not independently checked): native **99.6 % of characters / 96.0 % of words** found (pre.12: 98.9 / 95.0), Tesseract 98.5 / 93.4. The test pages are from the same book as the training pages, so this shows adaptation, not generalisation.
  - 12 magazine pages against ABBYY's text layer: character error 3.67 % (pre.12: 3.61 %), unchanged within noise; Tesseract 7.8 %.
  - Synthetic pages in 8 languages: mean error 0.030 % (pre.12: 0.068 %).
- Still weak: letter-spaced display titles between dither bars, table pages (fewer words than Tesseract), S-shaped wave lines. Recall figures do not penalise extra output.

Not solved: no hand-verified reference text; no real stamped scans; Windows/macOS builds are CI-only; package recipes unsubmitted; FADGI tables and a public TSA contract are open.
